newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Poll shows most Colombians trust no one.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows most Colombians trust no one.

text.p: An overwhemlming majority of Colombians have little or no trust in other people, a poll published on Sunday showed.
It said 85 percent of 2,170 participants in the survey answered "no" when asked, in general terms, if most other people were worthy of their confidence or trust.
Only 13 percent responded with a "yes" and 2 percent said they were unable to respond or did not know.
The survey, published in the Cambio 16 news magazine, was conducted in 30 provincial capitals by the National Consulting Centre on Dec. 17.

No margin of error was given for the poll. But Cambio 16, citing another survey conducted in February, said it indicated that Colombia was among the countries with the lowest level of trust anywhere in the world.

The February poll, dubbed the World Values Survey, showed that only 10.2 percent of Panamanians trusted other people. Other countries with a high degree of scepticism included Mexico, Puerto Rico and Bolivia.

The Cambio 16 poll gave no reason for the high level of distrust among Colombians. But the country, described in a recent World Bank report as the nation with the highest murder rate in Latin America, has been torn by political and drug- related violence for decades.

It also also boasts one of the world's highest kidnapping rates and has been described, by human rights groups and government officials alike, as a country where more than 95 percent of all crimes go unpunished.
